note: Literature confirms that absence of ectopia lentis (sparing of ciliary zonule and lens position) is a classic distinguishing ocular feature of Loeys-Dietz syndrome, including SMAD2-related disease, in contrast to Marfan syndrome.

evidence.text: Loeys-Dietz syndrome is caused by mutations in TGFBR1/2, SMAD2/3, or TGFB2/3, and unlike Marfan syndrome, no association is reported between LDS and the presence of ectopia lentis, which serves as a key distinguishing feature.

source.title: Differences in manifestations of Marfan syndrome, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, and Loeys-Dietz syndrome
source.quote: In contrast, no association is reported between LDS and the presence of ectopia lentis, a key distinguishing feature of MFS.

evidence.text: Across the spectrum of Loeys-Dietz syndrome including SMAD2, craniofacial features such as hypertelorism and the absence of ectopia lentis help differentiate LDS from related connective tissue disorders.
